scope.summary: Implement the trigger model (the event half of an interaction on a hotspot StudioLayer/frame) with a trigger inspector and the pointer/touch trigger subset: on click/tap; while hovering (auto-reverts on exit); while pressing (reverts on release); mouse enter/leave (no auto-revert); mouse down/up (press state machines, no auto-revert). Touch equivalents map to the same trigger primitives as their pointer forms.
acceptance_criteria: Pointer/touch trigger set with correct auto-revert semantics
expected_tests: argus: trigger inspector reachable via author_id; click/tap, hover, press, enter/leave, down/up
live: each pointer/touch trigger fires its interaction; hover/press auto-revert; enter/leave + down/up do not auto-revert
acceptance_criteria_original: pointer/touch trigger set with correct auto-revert semantics; touch maps to pointer primitives; author_id + manual entry

spec_clauses.spec_clause_text: [STU-PRO-004] A trigger is the event that fires an interaction on a hotspot `StudioLayer` or frame. The trigger set is normative and enumerated below; Studio MUST support the full set. Touch equivalents (tap, touch-down/up) map to the same trigger primitives as their pointer forms. | Trigger | Anchor | Fires when | |---|---|---| | On click / tap | [STU-PRO-005] | the hotspot is clicked (pointer) or tapped (touch) | | On drag | [STU-PRO-006] | the object is dragged, with continuous movement mapping (swipeable UI) | | While hovering | [STU-PRO-007] | the cursor is over the hotspot; auto-reverts on exit | | While pressing | [STU-PRO-008] | during click-and-hold / tap-and-hold; reverts on release | | Key / gamepad | [STU-PRO-009] | a key, key combination, or controller button is input | | Mouse enter / leave | [STU-PRO-010] | the cursor enters / exits the hotspot area, without auto-revert | | Mouse down / up | [STU-PRO-011] | press start / release, without auto-revert (press state machines) | | After delay | [STU-PRO-012] | a frame-level dwell timer elapses (splash screens, autoplay, timed states) | | Media timestamp / end | [STU-PRO-013] | a media-bearing layer reaches a set timestamp or ends playback | ### 3. Actions Actions are the response half of an interaction. Studio's action set spans navigation, overlays, variant switching, scrolling, external links, variable writes, conditionals, and media control, and actions compose (multiple per trigger, nestable under conditionals) so a single trigger can run a small runtime program.
| On click / tap | [STU-PRO-005] | the hotspot is clicked (pointer) or tapped (touch) |
| While hovering | [STU-PRO-007] | the cursor is over the hotspot; auto-reverts on exit |
| While pressing | [STU-PRO-008] | during click-and-hold / tap-and-hold; reverts on release |
| Mouse enter / leave | [STU-PRO-010] | the cursor enters / exits the hotspot area, without auto-revert |
| Mouse down / up | [STU-PRO-011] | press start / release, without auto-revert (press state machines) |

implementation_notes.naming: Vendor product names are provenance only. Studio ships Handshake-native names per [STU-SECTION-003].
implementation_notes.database: SurrealDB with the EventLedger is the only durable authority. SQLite, libSQL, Turso and PostgreSQL are forbidden, including in tests and dev caches.
implementation_notes.engine_split: GPU, WGSL and compute live in the studio-engine crate behind its traits. handshake_core must never gain a GPU dependency.
implementation_notes.routing: Navigation extends the existing address and bus seams. No new router.
implementation_notes.worktree: Code paths resolve against the WP-KERNEL-012 worktree, never main.

validator_focus: Confirm every acceptance row traces to a sentence in the cited spec clause carried in implementation_notes. A row with no spec basis is a fabrication.
Reject any row still carrying proof_target_status REQUIRED: it has no proof of its own.
Reject scaffold-only proof: at least one proof command must drive the executable runtime rather than a fixture the implementer authored.
Where the contract touches numeric parameters, confirm hard and soft bounds are stored as separate values and an unknown bound is stored as unknown, never mirrored.

resource_privacy_obligation.rule: Resources this contract reads, derives, caches or exports stay inside the authenticated operator's scope. No cross-identity read path may be introduced.
